angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 736,051 km at 14.74 pc = 0.67 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 67.8467 +/- 0.0601 mas (same row, RUWE 0.91): 14.74 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 1.058 +/- 0.019 solar radii from Delrez et al. 2021, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of HD 136352 c in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2021NatAs...5..775D/abstract): 736,051 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.87 +/- 0.04 solar masses from Delrez et al. 2021, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of HD 136352 c in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2021NatAs...5..775D/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5664 +/- 61 K from Delrez et al. 2021, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of HD 136352 c in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2021NatAs...5..775D/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Delrez et al. 2021, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of HD 136352 c in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2021NatAs...5..775D/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/hd-136352.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.329, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from a blackbody at the star's published temperature (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
